'''''Sporobolus africanus''''', or '''rat's tail grass''', is a [[Poaceae|true grass]] in the tribe [[Zoysieae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sporobolus africanus (Poir.) Robyns & Tournay {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:422594-1 |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

''Sporobolus africanus'' is known by many common names, including African dropseed, African dropseed grass, dropseed grass, Indian rat's tail grass, Parramatta grass, rat tail grass, rat's tail, rat's tail grass, rats' tails, ratstail, ratstail dropseed, rattail dropseed, rat-tail grass, rattail grass, rattailgrass, rush grass, smut grass, smutgrass, tough dropseed, tufty grass, and tussock grass.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Sporobolus africanus |url=https://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/media/Html/sporobolus_africanus.htm |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=keyserver.lucidcentral.org}}</ref> 

== Description ==
''Sporobolus africanus'' is an erect, stiff, tufted, perennial grass. Leaves are 20–40cm long and 1–4mm wide, in-rolled, scabrid, and olive-green. The panicle is 9-22cm long, with a long, densely-packed grey-brown inflorescence, bearing 2.2-3mm spikelets with a single floret.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2025 |title=Sporobolus africanus (Poir.) Robyns & Tournay |url=https://pza.sanbi.org/sporobolus-africanus}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=AgPest » Ratstail |url=https://agpest.co.nz/?pesttypes=ratstail |access-date=2025-08-23 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Connor |date=2000 |title=Sporobolus africanus (Poir.) Robyns & Tournay |url=https://floraseries.landcareresearch.co.nz/taxa/92dc6381-89b1-4b38-836c-83e39f4d3439}}</ref>

== Distribution ==

=== Native range ===
The native range for the species is southern and eastern Africa (from the Democratic Republic of Congo to South Africa), as well as Kenya, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Nigeria, Cameroon, Arabia, and Sri Lanka.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

In South Africa, it occurs in Free State, Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, Northwest, and the Northern, Western and Eastern Cape Provinces.<ref name=":1" />

=== Naturalised range ===
''Sporobolus africanus'' is naturalised in Madagascar, Philippines, Australasia (Papua New Guinea, New Zealand, and Australia (including Lord Howe I., Norfolk I., and Kermadec I.)), throughout the Pacific (Cook Is., Easter Is., Hawaii, Niue, Tokelau-Manihiki, French Polynesia, Mariana Is.), Atlantic Ocean islands (the Azores, Canary Is., Madeira, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, and St. Helena), and Indian Ocean islands (Mauritius and Réunion).<ref name=":0" />

== Habitat ==
''Sporobolus africanus'' typically grows in compacted soils and is well-suited to low-fertility.<ref name=":3" /> ''S. africanus'' is a grass of open areas, such as lawns and pastures, footpaths, parks, roadsides, disturbed sites, as well as native grasslands, open woodlands.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" />

== Ecology ==
In cool-temperate South African grasslands, ''S. africanus'' is often associated with ''Eragrostis curvula, Cynodon dactylon'' and ''Hyparrhenia hirta'', as well as herbs such as ''Walafrida densiflora, Solanum'' spp. and ''Wahlenbergia caledonica''.<ref name=":3" /> 

''Sporobolus africanus'' is a prolific seed producer with an average of 300 seeds per inflorescence and as many as 3,600 seeds per square metre.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" /> Seeds become sticky when wet, allowing them to attach directly to animals, clothing, and machinery.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Austin |first1=Peter |last2=March |first2=Nathan |last3=Johnson |first3=Kym |date=2011 |title=Weedy ''Sporobolus'' grasses – Best Practice Manual |publisher=Department of Primary Industries and Fisheries, Queensland Government |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328280009_Weed_Management_Guide_-_Weedy_Sporobolus_Grasses |doi=10.13140/RG.2.2.22862.31048 |access-date=19 March 2026 }}</ref> ''S. africanus'' also has a tendency to build up long-lasting seedbanks, which can be further enable their spread through the spread of mud by machinery.<ref name=":1" /> 

=== Invasiveness ===
''Sporobolus africanus'' is specifically seen as invasive in New Zealand, Hawaii, and Australia. 

In Australia, it arrived in the 19th century, either deliberately as a pasture plant our through seed contamination. It is largely an agricultural weed of pastures, given its low palatability that leads to a loss in productivity and reduced land values. It is an ecological weed in coastal areas and grasslands.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Palmer |first=W. A. |date=2016-01-25 |title=Sporobolus africanus (rat's tail grass) |url=https://www.cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/full/10.1079/cabicompendium.117302 |journal=CABI Compendium |volume=CABI Compendium |article-number=117302 |doi=10.1079/cabicompendium.117302|doi-access=free }}</ref>

In New Zealand, it naturalised in 1840, and has spread throughout the North Island andnorthern South Island.<ref name=":3" /> Its spread has impacted ''[[Anthosachne kingiana]]'' subsp. ''multiflora'', ''[[Austroderia splendens]]'', ''[[Daucus glochidiatus]]'', ''[[Echinopogon ovatus]]'' and ''[[Epilobium billardierianum|Epilobium billardiereanum]]'', as well as other lowland and coastal species.<ref>{{Cite web |last=De Lange |first=Peter James |last2=Gosden |first2=Jane |last3=Shannel P. Courtney |last4=Fergus |first4=Alexander J. |last5=Barkla |first5=John |last6=Beadel |first6=Sarah M. |last7=Champion |first7=Paul D. |last8=Hindmarsh-Walls |first8=Rowan |last9=Makan |first9=Troy |last10=Michel |first10=Pascale |date=2024 |title=Conservation status of vascular plants in Aotearoa New Zealand, 2023 |publisher=New Zealand Department of Conservation |issn=2324-1713 |url=https://rgdoi.net/10.13140/RG.2.2.11940.49288 |language=en |doi=10.13140/RG.2.2.11940.49288}}</ref>

On [[Hawaii|Hawaiʻi]], ''S. africanus'' is one of several invasive weeds threatening the native herb ''[[Bidens micrantha]]'' subsp. ''kalealaha'' and shrub ''[[Brighamia insignis]].<ref name=":3" />''

=== Natural enemies ===
Research was undertaken on natural enemies with potential to be used as biocontrol for ''[[Sporobolus]]'' sp. (including ''S. africanus'') in Australia.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Palmer |first=W. A. |last2=Yobo |first2=K. S. |last3=Witt |first3=A. B. R. |date=2008 |title=Prospects for the biological control of the weedy sporobolus grasses in Australia. |url=https://caws.org.nz/old-site/awc/2008/awc200812641.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the 16th Australian Weeds Conference |location=Cairns, Queensland |pages=264–266}}</ref> Species identified included 70 insects and 23 plant pathogens. The leaf smut fungus ''[[Ustilago sporoboli-indici]]'' and the wasp ''[[Tetramesa]]'' sp. showed potential, however, the wasp could not be reared in laboratory conditions, and the smut also impacted native Australian ''[[Sporobolus]].'' 

The moth ''[[Herpetogramma licarsisalis]]'' was found feeding on grasses, including ''S. africanus'' in 1968 on [[Maui]], [[Hawaii|Hawaiʻi]] (Davis, 1969).
